title: Blepharoplasty
scope: Functional upper eyelid blepharoplasty / blepharoptosis repair for visual impairment

children.text: Documented patient complaints justifying functional surgery (visual field interference, reading difficulty, looking through lashes)

sourceSpan.quote: Any procedure(s) involving blepharoplasty and billed to this contractor must be supported by documented patient complaints which justify functional surgery.

present: {date}: Patient reports difficulty seeing objects approaching from the side and must lift her eyelids to read.
negated: {date}: Patient has no visual complaints; desires a more rested appearance.
contradicted: {date}: Procedure requested for cosmetic reasons only.
paraphrased: {date}: Upper lid skin obstructs her upper vision, making driving and reading difficult.

children.text: Visual impairment caused by dermatochalasis, blepharochalasis, blepharoptosis or brow ptosis on examination

sourceSpan.quote: Dermatochalasis, including symptomatic redundant skin weighing down on the upper eyelashes (i.e., pseudoptosis) and surgically induced dermatochalasis after ptosis repair.

present: {date}: Exam: bilateral dermatochalasis with redundant upper lid skin resting on the lashes; MRD1 0.5 mm OU.
contradicted: {date}: Exam: normal upper lid position, MRD1 4 mm OU, no redundant skin.

children.text: Visual fields show at least 12 degrees or 30 percent superior field loss, with improvement when the lid is taped/elevated
children.suggestedFix: Attach taped and untaped visual field tests showing the superior field loss and its correction.

sourceSpan.quote: A minimum 12 degree or 30 percent loss of upper field of vision with upper lid skin and/or upper lid margin in repose and elevated (by taping of the lid) to demonstrate potential correction by the proposed procedure or procedures is required.

present: {date}: Visual field testing: 24 degrees superior field loss untaped OU, improving to within 5 degrees of normal with lids taped.
contradicted: {date}: Visual fields: 4 degrees superior field loss untaped; no meaningful change with taping.
paraphrased: {date}: Automated perimetry demonstrates a 35 percent upper field restriction that resolves when the lids are elevated with tape.

sourceSpan.quote: Photographs may be used to demonstrate the eyelid abnormality(ies) necessitating the procedures(s)

present: {date}: External photographs (frontal, primary gaze) obtained showing upper lid skin overhanging the lid margin.
